basis: Beta v5 H (round-3 oddities item 5; trace s16/betav5/traces/household_costs.md section 1). Under hfce_to_pq (beta v4) the 42.56 bn USD moved out of ZAF T went to P (28.35) and Q (14.21) and households kept paying for it, so education was 14.8% and health 9.3% of ZAF household budgets (v3 3.8% and 3.8%); BWA, GAB, GNQ and MUS copy ZAF as sole S05 donor and showed 11.5-14.4% education. Stats SA's 2022 HFCE by purpose (UN SNA table 3.2) puts education at 3.53% and health at 6.84% of HFCE. Under hfce_by_coicop, P and Q take their FIGARO 2022 D1 parts only up to the room under these shares times the ICIO HFCE total at purchasers' prices (config/s03/hfce_coicop_caps_2022.csv), less what households already buy from P or Q (all origins); the rest goes to the other services households buy (ICIO G, H49-H53, I, J58T60, J61, J62_63, K, L, M, N, R, S; not O, P, Q, T) in proportion to the ZAF households' purchases of each from ZAF industries, with VA and output moved the same way. C and G keep their totals (hard S03-Hhhecg) and the caps hold (hard S03-Hcoicop). Trade-off: P's VA stays at its ICIO value (8.9 bn), well below FIGARO D1 for P85 (23.8 bn EUR), since the extra pay would need a buyer and government consumption has no room (the first G4 version left G 57% above WDI). T itself stays at the paid-domestic-work value. A labelled source correction; no GTAP text covers it.
